text:
alexa: hey team — enterprise POC (JB Corp) reporting they can't reach the dedicated endpoint from their office network. they say their egress IPs are behind a pool of NATs that rotate daily. they want to know our recommended path to get them unblocked and if there are any pricing implications for static egress or temporary access
marco: thanks. do we know whether this POC used a Hosted API key or the Dedicated endpoint we provisioned?
tasha: they requested dedicated pool in the contract and gave the dedicated endpoint hostname in the intake sheet. so Dedicated, yes.
marco: ok. for Dedicated endpoints we require an IP allowlist on the endpoint side. FQDN allowlist is not supported for endpoint auth; we match source IPs.
priya: summary of options (short):
1) customer configures a static SNAT / Elastic IP on their NAT gateway and provides /32s or small CIDR ranges — we add to allowlist (best for security + simplest).
2) site-to-site VPN or VPC peering (Private deployment) — more effort but no public allowlist.
3) temporary test window — we can add their current observed egress ranges for up to 72 hours to validate connectivity, then remove them. needs support ticket and justification.
4) proxy/jump-host — we can provision a short-lived proxy for POC but it is manual and not typical for self-serve POCs (ops time + small infra fee).
alexa: buyer also asked: "will static egress cost more?" how to answer?
tasha: we charge Dedicated reserved capacity for pool + an optional networking egress static allocation add-on. static egress itself is billed as an add-on that covers the IP persistence and NAT mapping (one-time provisioning + small monthly). give sales a ballpark and we'll run a quote.
marco: to get them unblocked quickly we can do: open support ticket and add their current NAT ranges for 72h. need their public CIDRs (list of /32s preferred) and a point of contact. ask them to run this from a workstation inside their egress path:
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-dedicated-<redacted>" https://dedicated-us.rw-inference.com/v1/health
```
we'll tail logs and watch source IPs we see. share them back and then we can decide static vs vpn.
priya: network checklist to request from customer:
- public IPs (CIDR or /32 list)
- ASN if they're doing prefix translation
- whether they rotate SNAT addresses (freq)
- any outbound proxies (we need real source IPs)
- contact for firewall admin (email + biz hours)

alexa: customer sent a CSV with 8 IPs but mentions they rotate across 3 NAT boxes. they want a permanent solution — leaning toward static egress add-on or Private deployment.
tasha: ask customer if security/compliance requires no public IPs inbound at all. if so, Private (VPC) or on-prem package is the recommendation. Dedicated static egress is fine if inbound from known IPs is acceptable to their firewall team.
marco: next steps for us:
- propose adding temporary 72h allowlist to validate traffic (I can own this)
- if validated, sales to request static-egress add-on in the quote
- Priya to draft the exact allowlist format + sample firewall ACL we need

priya: sample acl snippet to send them:
```
# permit outbound flows to Redwood dedicated endpoint (TCP/443)
allow from 203.0.113.45/32 to any port 443 comment "RBW dedicated endpoint" 
# repeat per provided /32
```

alexa: buyer also asked about hostnames in allowlist (they prefer allowlist by hostname). can we support SNI-based match?
marco: not for Dedicated endpoints — we terminate TLS at our frontend and do not rely on SNI for auth allowlist. IP-based only. if they need hostname-based controls, recommend Private/VPC and egress via their managed NAT or proxy.

tasha: I opened an internal sales note for pricing: estimate + one-pager on static-egress add-on. CM: please include term (min 1mo) and infra fee. alexa to confirm with buyer if they will proceed after POC.

alexa: i'll ask for the exact NAT rotation cadence and the firewall admin contact, and request the 8 current IPs in /32 format. i'll also get permission to run the 72h test window.

marco: I created support ticket INC-2345 for the temp allowlist. tagging deploy-bot to note we may add a short-lived ACL entry.
deploy-bot: acl-change scheduled: INC-2345 -> apply temp allowlist 1793456890, auto-remove 1793676890 ; owner: marco.

tasha: if they want to test curl from their side, include this sample to confirm source IP we see:
```
# run from inside their office egress
curl -s https://ifconfig.me
# then curl our health endpoint with the dedicated key
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-dedicated-<redacted>" https://dedicated-us.rw-inference.com/v1/health
```

alexa: perfect. i'll follow up with the customer now and update here. thanks team :thumbsup:
marco: thanks. once we validate, we can finalize the quote flow with sales for static egress.
